title: Primitive integral operation realization with the specified strict towers
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Schemes $W$ are finite type over $k$, with small pro-etale sites and $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the derived categories of strict semilinear systems $\mathscr S_W$ and the actual adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ with unit $u$ and counit $e$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Use simultaneous inverse images $P_v$, proper direct images $S_p$, quasi-compact open extensions $J_j$ and derived tensor, as in [def-sf-integral-system-operations]. Restrict inputs and intermediate systems to the domain of [def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain]: derived-complete constructible integral inputs, normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, and common finite cohomological and Tor intervals. All conclusions below are restricted to expressions satisfying these intermediate-domain conditions.

For $A=P_v,S_p,J_j$ or the two-input tensor operation, there are specified natural isomorphisms
$$d_A(K_i):\mathcal L A(\mathcal R K_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\rm int}(K_i).$$
Here $v$ is separated finite type and $p$ proper; $A_{\rm int}$ is completed pullback or completed tensor [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], integral proper direct image [def-weil-derived-direct-image], or localized completed-ring open extension [lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison], respectively. For pullback and tensor, $d_A$ is the comparison of the strict total limit with the quotient-complex Roos formula, natural on flat-term K-flat representatives and their morphisms, using the natural Roos triangle and derived products [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. For direct image it is the comparison with the defining proper-image reduction tower, including its coefficient-restriction transitions. For open extension it is exactly
$$d_{J_j}(K)=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\mathcal L(r_j(K))^{-1},$$
where $r_j:\mathcal R(j_!K)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j\mathcal R K$ is the specified whole-system open reduction map; this identifies the realized open adjunction with the localized ringed-site adjunction.

For a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$, there is also a natural direct comparison
$$d_c(K):\mathcal L S_pJ_j\mathcal R K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!^cK,\qquad f=pj,$$
with exactly the functor and maps of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. For every $m\ge n\ge1$, its tower transition is $Rp_{*,m}j_!$ applied to $K_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n$, followed by the coefficient-restriction isomorphism of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars]. Thus $d_c$ identifies whole strict towers and their total limits, not just their evaluated objects. This assertion constructs primitive comparisons only; it asserts no expression-tree or generator coherence.

The specialized primitive input domains and the exact Lean comparison specification are named in [def-sf-integral-basic-realization-data]; their mathematical conditions are the ones stated above.

old_proof.text: For each integral input choose one flat-term K-flat representative $P$ (and $Q$ for a second input), using lem-pc-kflat-resolution. The reduction functor of lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus is represented by the single strict system $P_n=P\otimes_{\widehat R} (A_n)$, with $\tau^P_{m,n}=1\otimes(A_m\to A_n)$. Apply lem-pur-quotient-system-flat-models to the ringed small pro-etale sites: the whole-system pullback $P_v\mathcal R K$ is represented by $Z_v(P)_n=v^{-1}P_n$, and the whole-system tensor of $\mathcal R K,\mathcal R H$ by $Z_T(P,Q)_n=\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes_{A_n}Q_n)$. Their actual transitions are $v^{-1}\tau^P_{m,n}$ and $a\otimes b\mapsto\tau^P_{m,n}(a)\otimes\tau^Q_{m,n}(b)$. All these maps are defined before localization. For cochain maps $h:P\to P'$ and $g:Q\to Q'$, the equality $(h_n\otimes g_n)(\tau^P_{m,n}\otimes\tau^Q_{m,n})=(\tau^{P'}_{m,n}\otimes\tau^{Q'}_{m,n})(h_m\otimes g_m)$ follows on pure tensors; the inverse-image equality is $v^{-1}(h_n\tau^P_{m,n})=v^{-1}(\tau^{P'}_{m,n}h_m)$. Thus these are strict tower comparisons natural in the representatives, rather than unrelated identifications at each level.

old_proof.text: After termwise restriction to $\widehat R$-modules, let $Z$ be either strict tower from step 1. Countable products on these pro-etale sites are exact by lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact. Hence lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison gives a natural projection-compatible isomorphism $\rho_Z:\mathsf C(Z)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod Z_n\to\prod Z_n)[-1]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim Z$. Fix precisely its normalization: on a K-injective tower resolution $a:Z\to I$, use $\mathsf C(a)$ followed by the inverse of the kernel inclusion $\lim I\to\mathsf C(I)$ with zero shifted-product coordinate. By def-pur-integral-derived-operations and lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined, $\mathsf C(Z_v(P))$ and $\mathsf C(Z_T(P,Q))$ are the prescribed completed pullback and tensor. Define $d_{P_v}$ and $d_T$ by $\rho_Z^{-1}$ through the representative identifications of step 1. The hypotheses of lem-pur-flat-roos-functor-descent hold: the good representatives exist, their tower constructions preserve quasi-isomorphisms by lem-pur-quotient-system-flat-models, and products are exact. That lemma therefore descends these comparisons to natural isomorphisms on all derived input morphisms, including roofs; its uniqueness with the prescribed representative components makes them independent of resolution choices. This gives the required comparisons of functors and fixes the Roos maps, rather than choosing a filler of a triangle.

old_proof.text: For a proper $p$, retain its simultaneous derived system direct image from def-sf-integral-system-operations. The canonical evaluations and coefficient-transition comparisons of lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison and lem-pur-coefficient-system-unbounded-comparison identify its evaluation at $n$ with $Rp_{*,n}$, using the specified system resolution comparisons. In particular on $\mathcal R K$ its restricted tower has terms $\operatorname{Res}_nRp_{*,n}K_n$. If $\tau_{m,n}:K_m\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}K_n$ is the input quotient map, the output arrow is $Rp_{*,m}(\tau_{m,n})$ followed by $Rp_{*,m}\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}Rp_{*,n}$. This is the restriction comparison of lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars, with its defining resolution map. The unbounded system comparison includes the representative and transition equations, so these comparisons identify the whole restricted derived tower, not just its evaluations. These are exactly the terms and transition arrows specified in def-weil-derived-direct-image. Apply the functor $R\lim$ of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit to this whole-tower identification to obtain $d_{S_p}:\mathcal L S_p\mathcal R K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*K$. Naturality is the naturality of that system comparison followed by a functor; no separate choice of a map between homotopy-limit triangles is involved.

old_proof.text:
For a quasi-compact open $j$, use exactly the specified whole-system map $r_j(K):\mathcal R(j_!K)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_j\mathcal R K$ of lem-sf-integral-open-reduction-comparison. That statement applies because $K$ is derived complete and $\ell$ is invertible on the schemes; it asserts compatibility with every quotient transition, completeness of $j_!K$, and invertibility of the actual unit $u_{j_!K}$. Define
$$d_{J_j}(K)=u_{j_!K}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L(r_j(K))^{-1}.$$
The inverse of $\mathcal L(r_j(K))$ goes from $\mathcal L J_j\mathcal R K$ to $\mathcal L\mathcal R(j_!K)$, so the displayed formula has the required source and target. Both factors are natural isomorphisms. The cited node also identifies this precise comparison, including the unit and counit, with the localized completed-ring open adjunction. Thus the assertion about the open adjunction follows for these actual maps; no conclusion about faithfulness of evaluation is needed.

old_proof.text:
